blocks.title: Introduction and results
blocks.content: Quantum Geometry [@thiembook; @rovbook; @alrev] provides microscopic degrees of freedom that account for the black-hole entropy. The issue was raised in works by Krasnov [@krasentropy] and Rovelli [@roventropy]. The final quantum Isolated Horizon framework was introduced by Ashtekar, Baez, Corichi and Krasnov [@abk]. The framework describes a black-hole in equilibrium surrounded by a quite arbitrary space-time. blocks.title: The horizon quantum states
blocks.content: Our departure point is the quantum Isolated Horizon theory introduced in [@abk]. A classical (weakly) isolated horizon is a null, non-expanding world-surface of a space-like 2-sphere $S$, equipped with a null vector field of a constant self-acceleration. This idea gave rise to a new quasi-local theory of black-hole in equilibrium interesting also from purely classical point of view [@IH]. The local degrees of freedom of space-time geometry out of the horizon are not restricted. blocks.content:
